public_evidence.quote: Public website offers Texas household energy plans.
Public tariff lists one-year price-lock and insurance options.

private_insight.answer: The real friction is after the quote: people ask whether the final bill will match it. I want to compare price certainty messaging with insurance messaging, not simply attract more clicks.

public_evidence.quote: Public website describes scheduling software for operations teams.
Public buying guide describes manager evaluation and annual subscriptions.

private_insight.answer: Users love the scheduler, but the budget owner wants a security review before renewing. The journey must include that approval; adding user features alone may miss the blocker.

public_evidence.quote: Public website sells vanilla ice cream through independent grocers.
Public terms require distributor pallet orders.

private_insight.answer: Stores want smaller repeat orders. Distributor pallet minimums block them. The one vanilla smell complaint is not evidence of the main sales problem.

public_evidence.quote: Public site advertises implementation consulting and outcomes-based delivery.
Public page describes project approval, implementation, and acceptance.

private_insight.answer: We cannot add consultants this year. Any contribution target has to fit those ten people; reducing project hours is a scenario, not an established effect.

public_evidence.quote: Public website offers home-service appointment booking.
Public booking flow ends at appointment confirmation, before service completion.

private_insight.answer: The target is inquiry-to-booking, not completed jobs. Our internal dashboard calls both conversion, which is confusing. Completion must remain a separate transition.

public_evidence.quote: Public company catalog describes industrial products sold to manufacturers.
Public journey shows evaluation, pilot qualification, procurement, and delivery.

private_insight.answer: Procurement approval comes after technical pilot success. Marketing treats a successful pilot as a sale, but the buyer has not yet approved the budget.
